dedupe_keys.name: altair winprop wave propagation and radio network planning suite

description: WinProp is a suite of wave propagation models and radio network planning modules, originally developed by AWE Communications, a spin-off from the University of Stuttgart, then part of Altair's electromagnetic simulation portfolio with Feko, and now under Siemens after Siemens acquired Altair. It offers fast empirical and ray-tracing propagation models for rural, urban, indoor, industrial and tunnel scenarios, and network planning modules for almost every standard, including cellular networks up to 5G and LTE, Wi-Fi, broadcasting and TETRA. Altair presents it for radio coverage planning in heterogeneous networks that mix outdoor macro and micro cells with indoor pico and femto cells, for network roll-out and optimisation, comparing deployment concepts, evaluating installed antenna performance, coexistence analysis between networks and IoT deployments, with webinars on virtual drive testing. Its propagation engine was also licensed to iBwave for in-building design in 2007. Coverage: worldwide use. Format and access: commercial desktop software under Altair (Siemens) licensing, with webinars and trial access by request. Caveats: proprietary; accurate urban and indoor predictions require detailed building data. Simulation uses: coverage and capacity planning of mobile, broadcast and private networks, and assessing how building damage or site outages change coverage. Related records: Remcom Wireless InSite and Sionna are other ray-tracing tools, and iBwave Design embeds WinProp's engine.
